video_title: Game 4 PREVIEW: Pivotal Game 4 + Wemby Becoming a Villain

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The pressure on the Knicks in Game 4 at MSG
quotes.excerpt: I'd like to downplay that, but I cannot, because I do not want to... I can't quite bring myself
quotes.quote: It is the morning, actually the afternoon after here in New York. There is definitely a sobering effect. The city was euphoric 24 hours ago, and now I think there is some concern. I'd like to downplay that, but I cannot, because I do not want to. I can't quite bring myself to say the winner of Game 4 will win the series, mostly because home court has meant almost nothing. However, I know this is very basic: Game 4 is very important.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks fans are feeling the pressure of a playoff loss
quotes.excerpt: Knicks fans forgot what it was like to lose a playoff game. They were bounced in the first round.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Part of it is Knicks fans forgot what it was like to lose a playoff game. The Celtics had lost more recently than the Knicks. They were bounced in the first round. A 62-win team played like a 62-win team last night, and if you thought it was going to be easy, think again. The Spurs are going to put up a fight, and that fight might even include tossing around the face of your franchise and not getting called for a foul.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Yet, we are in the afternoon here. It is possible they could roll that as a foul.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's physical play and villain status
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama has no problem doing some dirty, dark art stuff. He's obviously got the elbow to Naz Reid
quotes.quote: The Spurs play extraordinarily physically. It has made me laugh quite a bit over the past month about all this pearl-clutching about how physical the Thunder were when they played the Spurs, when the Spurs do all the same stuff and then some. Victor Wembanyama has no problem doing some dirty, dark art stuff. He's obviously got the elbow to Naz Reid on his resume, which was a pretty dirty play. The play with Jalen Brunson last night, not as dirty a play, but certainly not a clean play. He has embraced being the subject of animosity from the fans here. Madison Square Garden for a long time has been the playground of the stars of the league. While the Knicks have been a laughingstock for basically this entire century, Kobe Bryant, Steph Curry, LeBron James, Kevin Durant, all the all the biggest stars would come in here and win games here and love playing here and love winning here. Victor Wembanyama obviously wants to be on the same level or above all those guys, and so coming to New York City and winning games is a part of that.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's fatigue and the importance of rest
quotes.excerpt: I am exhausted today. I'm sure that he was feeling fatigue today. I felt like watching him
quotes.quote: I think one of the biggest challenges for him, and I know this is a repetitive, but I can't undersell it: energy. That's exactly what happened last night. Okay, so now this is the last time there's only one game in between days. The rest of it will be two days, and he definitely benefited from the two days. Having the weekend, I am exhausted today. I'm sure that he was feeling fatigue today. I felt like watching him on the podium today, you could tell he was I thought he was a little fatigued.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's heavy minutes and conditioning
quotes.excerpt: He said running enough to where his hamstrings burned. You know, all the things he did.
quotes.quote: This is a recovery day for the heavy minutes guys, and they did tweak the rotation. His minutes were down a little bit through three quarters. Somebody asked him, I think it was after Game 3, somebody asked him about all the training he did this summer, whether it's with the monks or visiting Hakeem or visiting KG or whatever. What has he felt benefited him most from his summer training during his playoff run? And he said running enough to where his hamstrings burned. You know, all the things he did. Running enough to where he felt that burn in his hamstrings because he has pushed his minutes up. Obviously, the intensity is higher, and he said he's felt his hamstrings burning a lot during these playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's role in the Spurs' offense
quotes.excerpt: He comes out at the beginning of games, even if he's not in the paint, he tends to
quotes.quote: He comes out at the beginning of games, even if he's not in the paint, he tends to come out and shoot a lot in the first few minutes of the game, every game. And then he fades. Not that he's not involved, but he comes in and out of the game after that. He comes out with an intent to score a lot in the first few minutes of every game. It's why they seem to lead 15 to 5 every single game, no matter who they're playing. But when we got to the fourth quarter last night, it was Stefan Castle and De'Aaron Fox who hit the big shots late, hitting the free throws late. It was De'Aaron Fox getting in the lane, it was Dylan Harper getting in the lane and making plays.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' need for better ball movement
quotes.excerpt: They got a lot of credit for their dribbling and driving and kicking and stuff earlier in the
quotes.quote: I think one of the things that you're going to see, they talked about turnovers as they did their media on Tuesday, but I think you're going to see a lot about ball movement. They got a lot of credit for their dribbling and driving and kicking and stuff earlier in the series, but their ball movement in the second half dried up. Only five assists after halftime in Game 3. I think they need to get back to their ball movement.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown's offensive system and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: Mike Brown mentioned he didn't think guys were making quick enough decisions. Josh Hart talked about how they
quotes.quote: Mike Brown mentioned he didn't think guys were making quick enough decisions. Josh Hart talked about how they let the not just the Spurs, but the game, this also gets back to the free throws, slow them down. And that second quarter when they scored 42 points, they were playing fast. And a lot of times, you talk about playing fast, you think about transition points. You can play fast in half-court sets, too. Some of the Knicks' best possessions, that ball is ping, ping, ping, ping, ping. And when the ball is pinging like that, Victor Wembanyama can't sit in the back and direct traffic.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.excerpt: Mike Brown would somewhat routinely refer to their offensive system as random. It sounds like a football.
quotes.quote: When Mike Brown early in his career when he started going with the Cavs, the Cavs were not known for having a complex offense. It was mostly give the ball to LeBron James, and LeBron would sometimes go back and forth with his jab step. And people in Cleveland started calling it the stanky leg offense. Well, Mike Brown would somewhat routinely refer to their offensive system as random. It sounds like a football. All right, everybody go out. You know, just go out and run around. That's what random is. So I noticed yesterday, or maybe it was today, I saw the quotes from today, he was talking about their offensive system they were running, and their system is now called summertime. Or their play is now called summertime, which is a dressed-up word for random. Because because, you know, in summertime, like you're out with your buddies, you're not, you know, you're not running, you know, horns up or, you know, whatever 34 rubber.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The need for Cat to be more involved
quotes.excerpt: Cat's got to touch it. Cat's got to be involved. If you don't want to call specific plays
quotes.quote: Cat's got to touch it. Cat's got to be involved. If you don't want to call specific plays for him, then it's on Mike Brown to emphasize that. It's on Cat to be aggressive, demanding the ball, getting in position for the ball, and then it's and then it's teammates to get him involved, too. And then it's Jaylen Brown's team. It's Jaylen Brown's show. Jaylen Brown's the primary decision maker, the primary ball handler. It's on Jaylen Brown to make sure that Cat's involved because that benefits everybody.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of rebounding for Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: It's hard for him to rebound like that if he has to move around a lot.
quotes.quote: It's hard for him to rebound like that if he has to move around a lot. If, you know, he's he's sprinting to the corner, trying to get a contest on a on an open three, well, it's hard to do that then turn around and be in position to to grab the miss. But again, the Knicks' offensive rebounding in particular is a major, major challenge for the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of Victor Wembanyama's start
quotes.excerpt: First 30 seconds of the game, what does Victor look like? Is he running in cement?
quotes.quote: For me, it's two very simple things. Talked about it all the way back to the beginning of the series. First 30 seconds of the game, what does Victor look like? Is he running in cement, or is he yamming the ball through the basket? If it's the second one, like it was in Game 3, the Spurs are going to be in business. I suspect that's probably not going to be the case tomorrow.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA Draft as a trade deadline
quotes.excerpt: By the draft, they're either going to have traded Giannis, or they're going to be then deciding to
quotes.quote: Two weeks from right now. By the draft, they're either going to have traded Giannis, or they're going to be then deciding to build around Giannis. It's like A or B. This was the the line of demarcation of what they're going to do. So we got two weeks to see what's going to happen.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Miami Heat's trade assets for Giannis
quotes.excerpt: The Heat have a fine package. I would say that if Giannis winds up on the Heat
quotes.quote: The Heat have a fine package. I would say that if Giannis winds up on the Heat, it's for one of two reasons. It's either because he puts his thumb on the scale and says I'm only going to play for the Heat, which frankly to this point, Giannis has shown no sign to do any of that stuff with any of this stuff, and so I would not anticipate that happening. And the other part is if teams are just wary of outbidding Miami. Because I think if there's other teams that decide to that are the teams that have been discussed decide to get in the mix, I think they all have enough to outbid the Heat if they choose to actually say, we want to go down the road with Giannis and sign up to have a guy who's going to be on the team till he's 36, 37 with, you know, a gigantic contract on the books and some of the potential long-term downsides that could come with that.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: The value of Evan Mobley and Paolo Banchero
quotes.excerpt: Evan Mobley is more valuable than any of the stuff that Miami is giving up. Paolo Banchero is
quotes.quote: Evan Mobley is more valuable than any of the stuff that Miami is giving up. Paolo Banchero is more valuable than any of the stuff Miami is giving up. Now, perhaps Orlando looks at it and says, we'd rather have Paolo Banchero. We don't want to trade for Giannis. But if Orlando gets in the mix and says, we want to make a trade for Giannis, they're going to outbid Miami.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: The potential for a Giannis trade
quotes.excerpt: If the Cavs got in the mix with Evan Mobley, they're at way ahead of Miami. Jaylen Brown
quotes.quote: If the Cavs got in the mix with Evan Mobley, they're at way ahead of Miami. Jaylen Brown is very good, and if the Celtics choose to go that way, you know, that's a starting point that puts you pretty far ahead. Now, is it Jaylen Brunson for Giannis trade up? Is it Jaylen Brown and stuff? I'm not sure. I don't think the Celtics are trading for Giannis. I don't think that's the kind of move they're going to make. I don't think Jaylen Brown is going out in a deal like that. But again, this all goes back to the same conversation where Miami is sitting there. Miami is definitely interested. Miami has an okay offer, but Miami doesn't have the Trump offer. They already have Giannis on their team. So the question is, will somebody come in and outbid them?
